**2026-10-28.** A patch release that adds one feature: a timer's interval can come from a FEEL
expression, and a deployment can carry its own configuration for those expressions. Everything in
the v0.6.0 release notes applies. Every literal timer behaves exactly as before. The
snapshot format is unchanged, so an instance parked by a 0.6.3 engine resumes under 0.6.4. The
`q:` namespace change is additive.

## Added: timer intervals from FEEL

Until now every interval the engine scheduled was written into the model: a `PT10M` window, a
`PT30S` retry delay. A window that depends on the request, a decision or a stored value needed a
gateway per case, and a delay that should differ between a test cluster and production needed a
second archive.

Now the body of a `<timeDuration>`, `<timeDate>` or `<timeCycle>`, a `<q:timeout duration>`, and a
`<q:retry initialDelay>` or `maxDelay` can each be a FEEL expression. The rule is **literal first,
else FEEL**:

- a text that parses as an ISO-8601 literal is that literal, validated and scheduled exactly as
  before;
- a text that looks like a literal but is written wrong (`PT5X`, `P1M`, `2026-03-01`) keeps its
  load error, with the same code;
- any other text that parses as FEEL is an expression;
- anything else is a load error.

```xml
<bpmn:boundaryEvent id="WindowClosed" attachedToRef="AwaitDelivery">
  <bpmn:timerEventDefinition>
    <bpmn:timeDuration>if payload.window = null then config.defaultWindow else payload.window</bpmn:timeDuration>
  </bpmn:timerEventDefinition>
</bpmn:boundaryEvent>
```

An expression is evaluated **once, when its timer is armed**: when the token reaches a timer
catch, when a boundary's host activity parks (including the boundary a `<q:timeout>` creates), and
each time a `<q:retry>` backoff is armed. It sees the instance's variables at that moment, plus
`config`. A duration may be an ISO-8601 string or a FEEL days-and-time duration. A date may be an
instant string with a zone, or a FEEL date and time with an offset or zone. A cycle must be a
repeating-interval string. Only the instant the expression resolves to is stored, so a resume, a
replay, a restart or a replica hand-off reads that instant and never evaluates the expression
again. A loop that comes back to the timer arms it again, and evaluates it again.

## Added: deployment configuration, `config.<key>`

`package.yaml` gains `properties:`, a flat map that a timer expression reads as `config.<key>`:

```yaml
properties:
  defaultWindow: "${DEFAULT_WINDOW:PT10S}"   # env reference with a default
  retryDelay: "env:RETRY_DELAY"              # whole-value env reference
  startAfter: "PT1H"                         # a literal
```

The archive seals the text as written, so it is the same archive in every environment. The engine
resolves the references from its own environment when it activates the deployment. A reference
with no value and no default refuses the deployment (`SUTRA.DEPLOY.PROPERTY_UNRESOLVED`). Secret
references are refused, because every timer expression and the audit trail can read the
configuration. A timer **start event** may use an expression too, but it can read only `config`:
no instance exists when its schedule is armed. A `config.<key>` that `properties:` does not declare
is reported by `sutra lint` and `sutra package` and refuses the deployment
(`SUTRA.CONFIG.BPMN.TIMER_CONFIG_UNDECLARED`).

## When an expression cannot be armed

If the expression returns null, a value of the wrong type, an unparseable string, a negative or
calendar-length duration, or an instant with no zone, the instance fails **once** with
`SUTRA.RUNTIME.TIMER.EXPRESSION_INVALID`. `GET /sutra/instances/{id}` shows that code as
`failureCode`. The message names the timer, the expression and what it returned. There is no
default and no retry: `<q:retry>` does not count it, and an error boundary does not catch it. When
the timer is armed by the step that starts the instance, the request is refused with that code and
nothing is stored. On a start event, the deployment refuses to activate.

## Try it

`examples/delivery-window` waits at a receive task for a delivery, for as long as the order says,
or for `config.defaultWindow`. The book's *Retries, history, and schedules* chapter walks through
it step by step.

## Upgrading

Replace the image or the binary. Nothing in an existing package needs to change. One edge case:
a timer text that was not literal-shaped but was valid FEEL (a bare word such as `soon`) used to be
a load error, and now loads as an expression. `sutra lint` shows these.

## Install

```bash
docker pull ghcr.io/startr-trade/sutra:0.6.4
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/startr-trade/sutra/main/scripts/install.sh | sh -s -- --version v0.6.4
```

The library crates are on crates.io as `sutra-feel = "0.6.4"` and `sutra-dmn = "0.6.4"`.
